sql: SELECT count(*) FROM users
SELECT DISTINCT country FROM users
SELECT date_trunc('week', created_at) AS wk, count(*) AS n FROM users GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1 DESC LIMIT 100
SELECT provider, count(*) AS n FROM logins GROUP BY provider ORDER BY n DESC
SELECT u.id, p.plan FROM users u JOIN plans p ON p.user_id = u.id WHERE u.created_at >= now() - interval '7 days'
SELECT u.id, o.total FROM users u LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.user_id = u.id
SELECT provider, count(*) FILTER (WHERE verified) AS v, count(*) AS total FROM logins GROUP BY provider HAVING count(*) > 10
WITH weekly AS (SELECT date_trunc('week', ts) AS w, count(*) AS c FROM events GROUP BY 1) SELECT w, c, c - lag(c) OVER (ORDER BY w) AS delta FROM weekly
SELECT CASE WHEN age < 18 THEN 'minor' ELSE 'adult' END AS band, count(*) FROM people GROUP BY 1
SELECT coalesce(country, 'unknown') AS c, round(avg(amount)::numeric, 2) AS avg_amt FROM orders WHERE status IN ('paid','shipped') GROUP BY 1
SELECT * FROM (SELECT id, row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY tenant ORDER BY ts DESC) AS rn FROM sessions) s WHERE s.rn = 1
SELECT a.name FROM authors a WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM books b WHERE b.author_id = a.id)
SELECT t.day, t.total FROM metrics t WHERE t.day BETWEEN $1 AND $2 AND t.label IS NOT NULL ORDER BY t.day
SELECT array_agg(DISTINCT tag) FROM posts
SELECT id FROM a UNION ALL SELECT id FROM b
SELECT id FROM a INTERSECT SELECT id FROM b
SELECT greatest(a, b) AS hi, least(a, b) AS lo, nullif(a, 0) AS z FROM t
SELECT x IS TRUE AS a, y IS NOT FALSE AS b FROM t
SELECT ARRAY[1,2,3] AS arr, (SELECT max(z) FROM q) AS m FROM t
SELECT a, b, count(*) FROM t GROUP BY GROUPING SETS ((a),(b))
SELECT a FROM t ORDER BY a NULLS LAST
SELECT sum(n) OVER w AS running FROM t WINDOW w AS (ORDER BY d)
SELECT g AS day FROM generate_series('2026-01-01'::date, '2026-02-01'::date, '1 day'::interval) AS g
SELECT count(*) FROM public.users
SELECT percentile_cont(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY amount) AS median FROM orders
SELECT lower(trim(email)) AS e, split_part(email, '@', 2) AS domain FROM users
SELECT id FROM users ORDER BY id LIMIT 50 OFFSET 100
SELECT a.id, b.id FROM users a JOIN users b ON a.referrer_id = b.id
WITH a AS (SELECT 1 AS x), b AS (SELECT x + 1 AS y FROM a) SELECT y FROM b
SELECT extract(year FROM created_at) AS yr, count(*) FROM users GROUP BY 1
